answer.rationale: The mandate and low-cost quote make switching tempting, but memory_c2's summary omits any mention of delivery reliability under tight capacity — exactly the risk that matters with the line at 94% committed volume and zero buffer, and only 14 days to transition before contract lapse. Verifying c2's original record checks whether onboarding speed and invoicing accuracy claims also covered on-time delivery performance, which is the load-bearing fact for this decision. Given the short window and no slack for disruption, switching primary vendor now carries asymmetric downside if the new vendor stumbles during ramp-up. Memory_c4 shows the incumbent has moved on price and terms before when benchmarked against market rates, so negotiating leveraging the low-cost quote as leverage can likely capture much of the mandated savings without introducing a new, unproven supply chain under time pressure. This defers the higher-risk vendor switch to next cycle when it can be piloted as a second source or done with more runway, rather than as a forced primary swap.
